distance.method: VLBA trigonometric parallax of Orion Nebula Cluster stars

lines.label: Hα 656 nm
lines.context: the nebula’s red light comes from its hydrogen gas; Hα is the strongest visible line of recombining hydrogen

notes.text: The intense radiation of massive young stars makes the surrounding gas glow with a reddish light: nebulae of hot, ionized hydrogen called H II regions.
The gas of an H II region settles at an equilibrium temperature of about 9000 K.

distance.method: ESA/Hubble heic1310: “its precise distance is not known, but it is thought to lie just over 2000 light-years”; the image page lists 2500 ly and O’Dell et al. (2013) 740 (+400/−200) pc

lines.label: [N II] 658 nm
lines.context: red in the Hubble image: ionized nitrogen, radiated from the coolest gas, farthest from the star (F658N filter)

lines.label: [O III] 501 nm
lines.context: green in the Hubble image: ionized oxygen, farther from the star than the helium and closer than the nitrogen (F501N filter)

notes.text: A red giant expels its outer layers and exposes its hot core; ultraviolet light from the core makes the discarded material glow.
Planetary nebulae take their name from their roughly circular appearance through low-magnification telescopes; they have nothing to do with planets.

distance.method: approximate distance printed on the ESA/Hubble image page

nebulae.name: Cosmic Cliffs, NGC 3324 (Carina)
nebulae.type: star-forming region (edge of a gaseous cavity)

notes.text: The “steam” rising from the cliffs is hot, ionised gas and hot dust streaming away from the nebula under intense ultraviolet radiation.
